finding: A coordinated UnifiedDB/ClayGraph semantic-access lineage proposes replacing query-time global row scanning with provenance-bound semantic seeds, rebuildable graph access projections and an always-available possibility-conditioned assembly preprocessor. This is a falsifiable architecture hypothesis, not evidence that the system is already more accurate or faster than conventional databases/retrievers.
counterhypotheses: Conventional SQLite FTS5/BM25 or hybrid RRF may equal or outperform the semantic preprocessor after maintenance/rebuild costs are included.
Always-on preprocessing may improve apparent retrieval metrics while harming downstream task accuracy through compression/selection bias.
scientific_gate: No claim of superiority until preregistered matched baselines measure retrieval quality, counterevidence retention, stale-state errors, latency distributions, rebuild cost, context/token use and downstream outcome.
ancestry_policy: All four commits are one coordinated development lineage; do not count them as independent replications.
